The Nursing Process

The nursing process — assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation, evaluation (ADPIE).

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the five steps of the nursing process
  • Explain the purpose of each step
  • Give an example of the nursing process in practice

In simple words

The nursing process is a systematic, scientific way to give nursing care. It has five steps: assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation and evaluation — remembered as ADPIE.

It is cyclical — after evaluation, you reassess and start again. It ensures care is individualised and effective.

The five steps

Step What the nurse does
Assessment Collects data about the patient
Diagnosis Identifies actual or potential health problems
Planning Sets goals and chooses interventions
Implementation Carries out the planned care
Evaluation Checks whether goals were met

Example

A patient with fever:

  • Assess: temperature 39°C, flushed skin.
  • Diagnose: hyperthermia related to infection.
  • Plan: reduce temperature within 2 hours.
  • Implement: tepid sponging, antipyretic as ordered, fluids.
  • Evaluate: recheck temperature; if normal, goal met.

🔴 ADPIE order

Assessment → Diagnosis → Planning → Implementation → Evaluation. The process repeats as the patient’s condition changes.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Every patient — use ADPIE for every patient, every shift.
  • Care plans — write nursing care plans using the five steps.
  • Handover — structure handover around the nursing process steps.
  • Evaluation — check whether interventions worked; change the plan if needed.
  • Documentation — record each step so the team can follow the plan.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. The nursing process has five steps: assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation, evaluation.
  2. ADPIE is a cyclical, scientific method for individualised care.
  3. Assessment collects data; diagnosis identifies health problems.
  4. Planning sets goals; implementation carries out care.
  5. Evaluation checks whether goals were met.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Nursing diagnosis is different from medical diagnosis.
  2. Goals should be specific, measurable and time-bound.
  3. Evaluation leads to reassessment and plan revision.
  4. The nursing process is used by all nurses in all settings.

📌 Memory trick

ADPIE — “A Delicious PIe Eaten” — Assess, Diagnose, Plan, Implement, Evaluate.

60-second revision

  • Nursing process = ADPIE: assess, diagnose, plan, implement, evaluate.
  • Cyclical and scientific.
  • Assessment = data; diagnosis = problems.
  • Planning = goals; implementation = action.
  • Evaluation = did it work? then reassess.

Test yourself

ADPIE stands for:

Answer: A. ADPIE = Assessment, Diagnosis, Planning, Implementation, Evaluation.

Which step comes after planning?

Answer: B. After planning comes implementation (carrying out the care).

Nursing diagnosis identifies:

Answer: B. Nursing diagnosis identifies the patient’s actual or potential health problems.

Evaluation checks whether:

Answer: B. Evaluation determines whether the goals of care were achieved.

The nursing process is:

Answer: B. The nursing process is cyclical — it repeats as the patient’s condition changes.
